title: Redwood - CloudMart Marketplace Integration Technical Sync
next_steps: Redwood to share draft marketplace listing and reference architecture (Samir)
CloudMart to validate network/egress requirements and provide contact for marketplace onboarding (Priya)
Schedule joint demo run for marketplace listing UI and provisioning flow (Lina)
Exchange security questionnaire and SOC2 docs (Samir)
Agree on pilot timeline and success metrics (both teams)
action_items: Samir Patel: Share draft marketplace listing + reference arch doc (due: 2026-03-09)
Lina Chen: Prepare short demo script showing provisioning and private deployment options (due: 2026-03-11)
Priya Rao: Confirm CloudMart marketplace onboarding contact and network constraints (due: 2026-03-05)
Dave Kim: Run internal checklist on KMS/HSM and provide notes on required IAM roles (due: 2026-03-08)
summary: Partner technical sync to align on Redwood integration into CloudMart marketplace, discuss reference architecture options (hosted listing, dedicated offering, private VPC flow), and agree pilot next steps. Focus on onboarding process, security artifacts, billing/provisioning flow, and demo plan.
topics: reference architecture (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining; quick roll call?
[00:07] Nina: Nina here, CloudMart partnerships.
[00:10] Dave: Dave, platform eng.
[00:12] Priya: Priya, solutions.
[00:15] Samir: Great, Samir Patel from Redwood, Lina Chen - our SE, Jordan from solutions is on too. We're here to talk through the marketplace integration and the technical bits.
[00:28] Lina: I can kick off with a high-level of the three integration patterns we typically support — hosted listing where customers buy through CloudMart and we host, a dedicated/reserved model for larger accounts, and private VPC/on-prem for regulated customers.
[00:45] Priya: Quick Q — for the hosted listing, how does network egress work? We need to understand if traffic stays in-cloud vs crossing out, our compliance team will ask.
[00:55] Lina: Right, so hosted is our managed offering; traffic runs on Redwood's hosted infra. For CloudMart marketplace we can support region pinning so data doesn't leave region, but egress for certain customers could still be a concern. We'll include a network diagram in the reference arch. Sometimes the wording in the marketplace listing needs to be precise — folks mistake 'no egress' for 'no data leaving account'.
[01:18] Dave: That's helpful. For dedicated/reserved, do you provide a tenant on our VPC or is it co-located on your infra?
[01:26] Jordan: Dedicated can be two flavors — Redwood-managed dedicated pools that are isolated by tenant on our infra, or a private deployment where we run our control plane or an on-prem package in the customer's VPC. For CloudMart enterprise customers we often recommend the latter if they require strict controls.
[01:40] Nina: Marketplace listing needs clear callouts about which SKU maps to which deployment. Also billing: do you integrate with CloudMart billing so we can surface usage on the marketplace invoice?
[01:51] Samir: We have marketplace integrations before — we can do direct billing through CloudMart if the marketplace supports meter usage forwarding; otherwise we can provide monthly invoices. We'll need to map SKUs. We'll share the draft listing with SKU mapping.
[02:10] Priya: On security, we need SOC2, ISO, and KMS details. Can you support customer-managed keys?
[02:18] Lina: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported in private deployments, and for Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping. In hosted we offer envelope encryption and can work with HSM integrations on a per-customer basis. We'll attach SOC2 and our security whitepaper.
[02:34] Dave: Any gotchas on IAM roles or service accounts when provisioning via the marketplace?
[02:39] Samir: For the VPC/on-prem flow, we require a deployment breakout and a service account with specific roles; for marketplace provisioning we can use a provisioning lambda or our API. We'll include a sample IAM policy in the reference doc.
[02:54] Priya: Great. On the reference architecture, can you show how KV cache and prefix caching behave across tenants — we need to reassure customers about isolation and token leakage.
[03:04] Lina: Sure — note: the transcript might mis-hear KV as K-V cash in prior docs — but technically our KV cache is per model instance and per-tenant. For hosted we maintain strict isolation; for dedicated, cache is isolated to the dedicated pool. We'll diagram that.
[03:20] Nina: For the marketplace UX, we want to show one-click provisioning for hosted and a guided flow for private deployments. What's the typical time to provision?
[03:29] Jordan: Hosted is minutes, dedicated could take hours to provision depending on capacity, and private VPC can take days depending on network approvals. For the marketplace listing we can surface these timelines.
[03:44] Samir: Also important — rollout policies. Customers will want to pin model versions and have automatic fallback to a cheaper variant. We can show the model variant policy in the listing notes.
[03:56] Priya: Regarding observability, will CloudMart customers get access to Redwood Console metrics? How would that surface in the marketplace?
[04:04] Lina: We provide per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and tracing hooks. For marketplace customers we can offer a console link and different tiers of retention based on the SKU. We'll include screenshots in the demo.
[04:20] Dave: About the pilot: we want a small alpha customer to run a 4-week trial. What metrics should we measure?
[04:27] Samir: Latency p95, per-token cost, correctness on a set of eval prompts, uptime, and rollout rollback time. We'll propose a short eval harness.
[04:40] Nina: Sounds good. A couple of specifics — CloudMart requires that partner listings include a security section and an integration checklist. Can you provide a checklist we can include?
[04:49] Samir: Absolutely. We'll create a marketplace checklist covering network, KMS, SSO, provisioning, and billing.
[04:58] Priya: For SSO/SAML and RBAC, do you support SCIM provisioning?
[05:03] Lina: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning in enterprise accounts. We'll note any limitations.
[05:11] Dave: On the technical side, if a customer chooses quantization for cost, can we show CPU/GPU requirements per variant? Some customers will ask for that.
[05:20] Jordan: Yes, our Optimize tool suggests quantization profiles and expected throughput/latency per hardware class — we'll include the typical profiles for the models we propose to list.
[05:33] Samir: One small caveat — when we reference third-party infra in the marketplace copy, we need to be careful about naming. Some customers confused 'CloudVendorX' in early drafts.
[05:43] Nina: Noted. We'll stick to neutral phrasing.
[05:47] Lina: For the joint solutions page, we can propose two reference architectures: 1) Quick-start hosted integration for SMBs, 2) Enterprise reference with VPC, KMS, and CAN/PCI notes. We'll attach diagrams.
[06:00] Priya: Can you include a sample CloudFormation/Terraform snippet for provisioning? That speeds internal review.
[06:06] Jordan: Yes, we'll produce a Terraform module sample for marketplace provisioning and a minimal CFN for one-click host flow.
[06:14] Dave: On data residency: some customers in EU will insist data remains in EU region. Can the hosted listing restrict hosting to eu-west regions only?
[06:22] Lina: Yes — regional constraints are supported. We'll mention region pinning in the listing and reference arch.
[06:30] Nina: Ok, timeline recap — we want the draft listing and reference arch by next week, demo the following week, and security docs this week if possible.
[06:38] Samir: We'll target the draft listing by 2026-03-09, Lina will prepare demo script by 2026-03-11, and we'll push security artifacts ASAP.
[06:50] Priya: One operational question — for billing meters, do you expose per-token usage via API so CloudMart can ingest usage for billing?
[06:58] Samir: We can export usage via a metering API or periodic CSV. For direct marketplace billing, we typically integrate meter forwarding if the marketplace supports it. We'll outline options.
[07:10] Dave: Anything else on SLA? We need clear statements for uptime for hosted and SLA terms for dedicated.
[07:16] Samir: We offer SLA-backed uptime for Dedicated and best-effort for hosted; details in the partner agreement. We'll forward the SLA doc.
[07:24] Nina: Good. Let's wrap with next steps and owners.
[07:28] Samir: Recap — Samir share draft listing & ref arch; Lina demo script; Priya identify marketplace contact; Dave KMS/IAM notes; agree pilot timeline. We'll set up the demo for week of 2026-03-16.
[07:45] Nina: Thanks everyone.
[07:47] Samir: Thanks, bye.
[07:49] [end of recording]
